by Mike Bufano, Open Source Programs Office

In 2006, Google formalized its relationship with the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) as one of its first corporate sponsors and twenty years later, that partnership continues through ongoing sponsorship and upstream contributions.

At the core of our collaboration is a shared belief in "The Apache Way" and its principles of open, vendor-neutral, and community-led development. From the early days of corporate open source to modern machine learning and open data systems, Google and ASF communities have collaborated on widely used open source software.

Shaping how Google does open source

When we established Google’s open source contribution workflow, we drew on established ASF practices. Both our Individual and Corporate Contributor License Agreements (CLAs), which external developers sign before contributing to a Google-owned open source project, are based on the ASF’s CLAs.

The Apache 2.0 license also remains Google’s preferred open source license for code. Alongside our traditional software releases, we also use Apache 2.0 for open hardware designs and open models like Gemma 4.

Co-engineering upstream and in the cloud

Across Google Cloud, our engineering teams contribute code upstream alongside Apache project communities and build managed services directly around those open standards:

  • Google Cloud Dataflow & Apache Beam: Drawing on Google’s internal Flume and Dataflow systems, Google donated the original Dataflow SDK and runners to the Apache Incubator in 2016 to help establish Apache Beam as a vendor-neutral open standard for unified batch and stream processing.
  • Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Airflow & Apache Airflow: Managed workflow orchestration built on Apache Airflow, helping engineering and data teams author, schedule, and monitor complex pipelines.
  • Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Spark & Apache Spark: Managed big data and analytics processing built on Apache Spark, running directly on Google’s cloud infrastructure.
  • Google BigQuery & Apache Iceberg: Support for the Apache Iceberg open table format to power large-scale analytics and machine learning datasets.

Setting the Platinum standard

Google has invested in the long-term health of open source foundations from the start. When the ASF first established its corporate sponsorship tiers, Google became the first Platinum Sponsor.

Early Google engineers and open source advocates worked closely with ASF maintainers to build the organizational and technical bridge between Google and the foundation. Today, Google maintains Platinum sponsorship through targeted funding and Google Cloud infrastructure contributions that support the ASF’s day-to-day technical operations.

That sponsorship pairs with everyday participation in ASF projects. Many Googlers serve upstream as ASF committers and Project Management Committee (PMC) members, maintaining code and stewarding projects alongside contributors across ASF communities. The ASF has also been a mentoring organization in Google Summer of Code (GSoC) for over 20 years, working with us to welcome and mentor new open source contributors around the world.

The next 20 years: AI, open data, and beyond

Looking ahead to the next two decades, much of our shared work sits at the intersection of open data, cloud infrastructure, and artificial intelligence.

Projects like Apache Iceberg are widely used in modern analytics and machine learning workflows, while using the Apache 2.0 license for open models helps bring permissive licensing to a new generation of tools.

Thank you to the developers, committers, PMC members, and maintainers who keep the Apache Software Foundation strong. Here’s to 20 more years of building together.
